Palworld isn't as bad as some game journalist make it out to be, let alone Twitter. Many have compared it to Pokemon due to its creature capture mechanics, or Breath of the Wild due to its open world. However, I'd argue this title is more like Ark Survival, but with its own twist. It definitely makes for an enjoyable experience more than it comes off as just a parody or "rip-off."

First, lets get into the pros of the game itself. For early acess, the graphics are rather stunning, even just running them around high settings. Now I would recommend players have at least 32gb of Ram if they were to start playing around early access. Especially with the game running on the Unreal Engine 5. While it can still run on 16gb minimum, you'll want to adjust your settings a bit before playing. Though there's a chance things are prone to change upon full release.

Next we have the pal designs themselves. While many argue some designs are too close with official Pokemon designs, I find them to still be distinct enough to be their own. Sure, its easy to point to Lamball and compare it to Wooloo, or or Direhowl to Lycanrock. However, I'd also like to make the argument that there's only so much you can do with creature designs, especially if they're derived or inspired by real life animals. There also comes the argument that the designs themselves are likely parody, poking fun at how easy or generic some Pokemon designs are. (This is coming from a life long Pokemon fan)

Third we have world design. I like the many different sections of Palpagos Island, and there's certainly many places you could build a base. I often find myself wishing I could build more than just three bases in my own save, especially if I have friends who join me through Co-Op. What can I say. I'm a huge sucker for scenery when it comes to building a base and exploring.

Fourth would be the game's soundtrack, The music for both capture, enemies, and even the title screen are very nice. I can only imagine what others tracks could be added in the near future. Perhaps we could get some over world tracks in the future. It certainly would be a nice touch for sure!

Now here comes the unfortunate part of the review, the cons. This game is still in Early Access, so I'm sure many of these are still being worked on and are bound to change before release. With that being said, I wouldn't try to take these section too heavily.

First we have the Pal's AI. Within the base, I've found many Pals who can't seem to find there way to task, or often have moved to an opposite task entirely after leaving base. No just that, but I've found times were the Pals refuse to go up stairs and ramps, limiting the ways I can build my base. While this issue has slightly improved with the 2.0.6 Patch of the game, its still got much work to be done.

Second has to do with the Palbox. Me and many other plays wish there was a better way to assign task to Pals within the base. I strongly feel this would not only elevate some players' frustrations, but could help maintain keeping Pals on task with the work assigned to them. Removing the need to constantly pick them up and throw them at a desired work station. If not by the Palbox, then it'd be nice to see this through the Podium.

Thirdly we have the map of Palego Island. While the map itself is spacious and has much to enjoy, I still find some spots that either feel too empty or lack a for of variety. The island would favor from some types of greenery and biomes. Though there's a chance we could see this in future maps, whether by patches or potential DLC. Could you imagine exploring a dark forest or cave with glowing fauna? I can only imagine how it'd look! Both in Palworld and the UE5 engine.

In conclusion, the game holds a lot of potential. I can't wait to see what the team at Pocket Pair has to bring, and I hope they continue to make more great games after this one. Palworld is the first game I've played from their library, and I certainly was't disappointed! I love being able to play through its early development, and getting to see all the new features that come out. Can't wait for Palworld's full release!

Pokemon who?  I collect pals now.

Kind of a weird concept that sort of hits you in the face when you first start.  The story begins as being pretty much nonexistant, zero context, and a vague compulsion to catch pals and build a base.  You don't really know the "why" behind anything unless you explore a lot.  Which is mildly frustrating but also keeps the game intriguing.  I feel like the main theme of the game comes down to morality and ethics.  What kind of pal-keeper are you?  Where do you draw the line?

Personally, I'm loving this game so far.  It looks great, the gameplay isn't overly complex (tho it helps if you're familiar with Pokemon).  I love the fact that the pals are completely interactive.  They follow you around, construct and defend your base, you can spoil them, eat them, ride them, give them orders.  Hell, you can even catch and enslave humans!  There's no shortage of things to do in Palworld.  If you don't feel like crafting, you can catch pals, unlock new areas, or loot dungeons.  Overall, Palworld is a solid game, and I really love it!
It's all those bad island crafting games with a huge world to explore...but now you're also a ruthless "Palemon" trainer/monster of a slave driver.
Fun and a Go at your pace game.
